what_its_for: Ferric iron is used to treat iron deficiency anemia, a condition where your body does not have enough iron to make healthy red blood cells. This can cause tiredness, weakness, pale skin, and shortness of breath. Your doctor may also prescribe it if you have chronic kidney disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or heavy menstrual bleeding that has led to low iron levels.
how_to_take: If you are taking ferric iron as a CAPSULE or TABLET (such as Accrufer): Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take it on an empty stomach, either 30 minutes BEFORE a meal or 2 hours AFTER a meal for best absorption. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsule. If you are receiving ferric iron as an INJECTION or IV INFUSION: This will be given to you by a nurse or doctor in a clinic or hospital. You do not need to do anything special at home for injections.
dosing: Dosing depends on the specific type of ferric iron and your medical condition. A common oral dose for adults (Accrufer) is 30 mg twice daily (one capsule in the morning and one in the evening). For IV forms, your doctor will calculate the dose based on your weight and how low your iron levels are. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of your oral ferric iron supplement, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still far from your next scheduled dose. If your next dose is coming up soon, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For IV doses given in a clinic, call your doctor or clinic to reschedule your appointment as soon as possible.
storage: Store oral capsules or tablets at room temperature (between 68°F and 77°F or 20°C and 25°C). Keep them in a dry place away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. IV forms are stored and handled by your healthcare team — you do not need to worry about storing those at home.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking iron supplements at the same time as antacids, calcium supplements, or dairy products (like milk or cheese) because these can block your body from absorbing the iron properly. Wait at least 2 hours between taking iron and these products. Avoid drinking coffee, tea, or cola close to the time you take your iron, as these can also reduce absorption. Do not take more than the prescribed dose — too much iron can be harmful. Avoid taking other iron supplements or multivitamins with iron unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe allergic reaction signs such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness (especially after an IV infusion). Also call your doctor if you notice: severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that does not go away; black, tarry, or bloody stools (this can sometimes be from iron but can also signal bleeding); chest pain or rapid heartbeat; extreme fatigue that is getting worse instead of better; or signs of iron overload such as joint pain, stomach pain, or darkening of the skin.
when_it_works: You may start to feel less tired and have more energy within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment, but it usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to see a significant improvement in your blood iron levels. Your doctor will check your blood tests regularly to track your progress. It is important to keep taking the medication even if you start feeling better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Iron deficiency is common during pregnancy. Ferric iron supplements may be recommended by your doctor. Talk to your doctor before starting any iron supplement while pregnant or breastfeeding. CHILDREN: Some ferric iron products are not approved for children. Always check with your pediatrician before giving iron supplements to a child. ELDERLY: Older adults can take ferric iron but may be more sensitive to stomach side effects. Start with the lowest effective dose as directed by your doctor. KIDNEY DISEASE: Certain IV ferric iron products are specifically designed for people with chronic kidney disease. Your doctor will choose the safest form for you. ALLERGIES: Tell your doctor about all your allergies before starting treatment, especially if you have had a reaction to any iron product in the past.
